manifest.title: The Immerman–Szelepcsényi Theorem

inputs.abstract: We prove [$\mathrm{NL}=\mathrm{coNL}$](paper.html#m24) by inductive counting on finite configuration graphs. The proof constructs a nondeterministic Turing machine that generates paths and census witnesses sequentially, halts on every branch, and uses logarithmic space. The argument includes correctness of the count sequence and space bounds for the compiled counting machine. Machine classes come from [lax-434930](https://laxarchive.org/lax-434930/).

concepts.title: Bounded machine configurations
concepts.description:
A configuration using at most $s$ work cells consists of a control state,
an input-head position, a work-head position, and $s$ work symbols.
Cells beyond this prefix are blank.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434930.SpaceMachines
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

/-!
---
title: Bounded machine configurations
type: definition
---
A configuration using at most $s$ work cells consists of a control state,
an input-head position, a work-head position, and $s$ work symbols.
Cells beyond this prefix are blank.
-/

namespace Lax362205.BoundedConfigurations

open Lax434930.SpaceMachines

structure Config (M : Machine) (n s : ℕ) where
  state : M.Q
  inputHead : Fin (n + 2)
  workHead : Fin s
  tape : Fin s → M.Γ
  deriving Fintype

def expand {M : Machine} {n s : ℕ} (c : Config M n s) : M.Config :=
  ⟨c.state, c.inputHead.val, c.workHead.val,
    fun i => if h : i < s then c.tape ⟨i, h⟩ else M.blank⟩

end Lax362205.BoundedConfigurations

concepts.title: Correctness of vertex classification
concepts.description:
With the correct current count, a vertex has a valid positive or negative
classification exactly according to its membership in the next layer.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.Counting

/-!
---
title: Correctness of vertex classification
type: lemma
---
With the correct current count, a vertex has a valid positive or negative
classification exactly according to its membership in the next layer.
-/

namespace Lax362205.Classification

open Lax362205.Reachability Counting

axiom correct {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a v : Fin N) (k : ℕ) (b : Bool) :
  Classify G a k (layer G a k).card v b ↔
    (b = true ↔ v ∈ layer G a (k + 1))

end Lax362205.Classification

statements.signature:
correct : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax362205.Reachability.Graph N) (a v : Fin N) (k : Nat) (b : Bool),
  Iff (Lax362205.Counting.Classify G a k (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a k).card v b)
    (Iff (Eq b Bool.true) (SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a (instHAdd.hAdd k 1)) v))

concepts.title: Counting on the configuration graph
concepts.description:
For every terminal accepting configuration, certify that it cannot be
reached from the initial configuration. The implementation must generate
the witnesses sequentially; this predicate alone makes no space claim.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.ConfigurationGraph
import Lax362205.Counting

/-!
---
title: Counting on the configuration graph
type: definition
---
For every terminal accepting configuration, certify that it cannot be
reached from the initial configuration. The implementation must generate
the witnesses sequentially; this predicate alone makes no space claim.
-/

namespace Lax362205.ConfigurationCounting

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines
open Lax362205.BoundedConfigurations Lax362205.ConfigurationGraph Counting

def RejectsByCounting (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : Config M w.length s, expand a = M.initial →
    M.Terminal w (expand b) → M.accept b.state = true →
    NonreachCertificate (graph M w s) (numbering M w.length s a) (numbering M w.length s b)

end Lax362205.ConfigurationCounting

concepts.title: The bounded configuration graph
concepts.description:
Vertices are configurations whose work tape has a fixed finite bound.
Edges are machine transitions. Acceptance is reachability from the initial
configuration to a terminal accepting configuration. The search predicate
replaces reachability by the recursive finite graph test.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.BoundedConfigurations
import Lax362205.Reachability
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.EquivFin
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

/-!
---
title: The bounded configuration graph
type: definition
---
Vertices are configurations whose work tape has a fixed finite bound.
Edges are machine transitions. Acceptance is reachability from the initial
configuration to a terminal accepting configuration. The search predicate
replaces reachability by the recursive finite graph test.
-/

namespace Lax362205.ConfigurationGraph

open scoped Classical

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines BoundedConfigurations Reachability

/-- Label all bounded configurations consecutively from zero. -/
noncomputable def numbering (M : Machine) (n s : ℕ) :
    Config M n s ≃ Fin (Fintype.card (Config M n s)) := Fintype.equivFin _

/-- Connect two numbered configurations exactly when the machine can move from the first to the second. -/
noncomputable def graph (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) :
    Graph (Fintype.card (Config M w.length s)) :=
  fun a b => decide (M.Step w (expand ((numbering M w.length s).symm a))
    (expand ((numbering M w.length s).symm b)))

/-- Some accepting terminal configuration is reachable from the initial configuration within the tape bound. -/
def AcceptsBounded (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : Config M w.length s,
    expand a = M.initial ∧ M.Terminal w (expand b) ∧ M.accept b.state = true ∧
    Reachable (graph M w s) (numbering M w.length s a) (numbering M w.length s b)

/-- The finite reachability search finds a path from the initial configuration to an accepting terminal one. -/
def SearchAccepts (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : Config M w.length s,
    expand a = M.initial ∧ M.Terminal w (expand b) ∧ M.accept b.state = true ∧
    search (graph M w s) (Nat.clog 2 (Fintype.card (Config M w.length s)))
      (numbering M w.length s a) (numbering M w.length s b) = true

end Lax362205.ConfigurationGraph

concepts.title: Inductive counting certificates
concepts.description:
The $k$th reachable layer contains vertices at distance at most $k$ from the
source. A census lists distinct reachable vertices and their path witnesses.
Given the correct census size, a negative classification checks that no
listed vertex has an edge to the target. A counting step classifies every
vertex and counts the positive answers.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.Reachability
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset

/-!
---
title: Inductive counting certificates
type: definition
---
The $k$th reachable layer contains vertices at distance at most $k$ from the
source. A census lists distinct reachable vertices and their path witnesses.
Given the correct census size, a negative classification checks that no
listed vertex has an edge to the target. A counting step classifies every
vertex and counts the positive answers.
-/

namespace Lax362205.Counting

open scoped Classical

open Lax362205.Reachability

/-- The vertices reachable from `a` using at most `k` directed edges. -/
noncomputable def layer {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k : ℕ) : Finset (Fin N) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun v => Within (fun u v => G u v = true) k a v)

/-- A set of `c` distinct vertices, each reachable within `k` steps. -/
def Census {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k c : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin N)) : Prop :=
  S.card = c ∧ ∀ v ∈ S, Within (fun u v => G u v = true) k a v

/-- A positive answer supplies a path; a negative answer supplies a census that has no edge to `v`. -/
def Classify {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k c : ℕ) (v : Fin N) : Bool → Prop
  | true => Within (fun u v => G u v = true) (k + 1) a v
  | false => ∃ S, Census G a k c S ∧ v ≠ a ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, G u v = false

/-- Classify every vertex for the next layer and count exactly `d` positive answers. -/
def CountStep {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k c d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ answers : Fin N → Bool, (∀ v, Classify G a k c v (answers v)) ∧
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => answers v = true)).card = d

/-- Start with the source alone and certify the size of each successive reachable layer. -/
def CountTrace {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (counts : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  counts 0 = 1 ∧ ∀ k < N, CountStep G a k (counts k) (counts (k + 1))

/-- A certified sequence of layer counts whose final census omits the target `b`. -/
def NonreachCertificate {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a b : Fin N) : Prop :=
  ∃ counts, CountTrace G a counts ∧
    ∃ S, Census G a N (counts N) S ∧ b ∉ S

end Lax362205.Counting

concepts.title: Correctness of one counting step
concepts.description:
Starting from the correct layer size, valid classifications produce exactly
the size of the next layer. Such classifications exist.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.Counting

/-!
---
title: Correctness of one counting step
type: lemma
---
Starting from the correct layer size, valid classifications produce exactly
the size of the next layer. Such classifications exist.
-/

namespace Lax362205.CountingStep

open Lax362205.Reachability Counting

axiom correct {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k d : ℕ) :
  CountStep G a k (layer G a k).card d ↔ d = (layer G a (k + 1)).card

end Lax362205.CountingStep

statements.signature:
correct : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax362205.Reachability.Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k d : Nat),
  Iff (Lax362205.Counting.CountStep G a k (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a k).card d)
    (Eq d (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a (instHAdd.hAdd k 1)).card)

concepts.title: Correctness of the count sequence
concepts.description:
The initial layer consists of the source. Inductive counting certifies
exactly the successive layer sizes, including the final size after $N$ steps.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.Counting

/-!
---
title: Correctness of the count sequence
type: lemma
---
The initial layer consists of the source. Inductive counting certifies
exactly the successive layer sizes, including the final size after $N$ steps.
-/

namespace Lax362205.CountingTrace

open Lax362205.Reachability Counting

axiom correct {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (counts : ℕ → ℕ) :
  CountTrace G a counts ↔ ∀ k ≤ N, counts k = (layer G a k).card

end Lax362205.CountingTrace

statements.signature:
correct : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax362205.Reachability.Graph N) (a : Fin N) (counts : Nat → Nat),
  Iff (Lax362205.Counting.CountTrace G a counts)
    (∀ (k : Nat), instLENat.le k N → Eq (counts k) (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a k).card)

concepts.title: Logarithmic space for inductive counting
concepts.description:
For a machine using logarithmic space, a nondeterministic machine implements
its configuration counting predicate in logarithmic space. Vertices and
bounded paths are generated sequentially. Every branch halts.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.ConfigurationCounting
import Lax434930.SpaceBounds

/-!
---
title: Logarithmic space for inductive counting
type: lemma
---
For a machine using logarithmic space, a nondeterministic machine implements
its configuration counting predicate in logarithmic space. Vertices and
bounded paths are generated sequentially. Every branch halts.
-/

namespace Lax362205.CountMachine

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines Lax434930.SpaceBounds
open ConfigurationCounting

axiom implement (M : Machine) (c : ℕ) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hM : ∀ w, M.UsesSpace w (c * logSpace w.length)) :
  ∃ (d : ℕ) (D : Machine), 0 < d ∧
    (∀ w, D.HaltsOn w ∧ (D.Accepts w ↔ RejectsByCounting M w (c * logSpace w.length))) ∧
    ∀ w, D.UsesSpace w (d * logSpace w.length)

end Lax362205.CountMachine

statements.signature:
implement : ∀ (M : Lax434930.SpaceMachines.Machine) (c : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 c →
    (∀ (w : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Word),
        M.UsesSpace w (instHMul.hMul c (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.logSpace (List.length w)))) →
      Exists fun d =>
        Exists fun D =>
          And (instLTNat.lt 0 d)
            (And
              (∀ (w : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Word),
                And (D.HaltsOn w)
                  (Iff (D.Accepts w)
                    (Lax362205.ConfigurationCounting.RejectsByCounting M w
                      (instHMul.hMul c (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.logSpace (List.length w))))))
              (∀ (w : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Word),
                D.UsesSpace w (instHMul.hMul d (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.logSpace (List.length w)))))

concepts.title: Exact censuses enumerate the whole layer
concepts.description:
A census of reachable vertices with the correct cardinality contains every
vertex of the layer. Distinctness is enforced by the finite-set representation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.Counting

/-!
---
title: Exact censuses enumerate the whole layer
type: lemma
---
A census of reachable vertices with the correct cardinality contains every
vertex of the layer. Distinctness is enforced by the finite-set representation.
-/

namespace Lax362205.ExactCensus

open Lax362205.Reachability Counting

axiom complete {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin N)) :
  Census G a k (layer G a k).card S → S = layer G a k

end Lax362205.ExactCensus

complete : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax362205.Reachability.Graph N) (a : Fin N) (k : Nat) (S : Finset (Fin N)),
  Lax362205.Counting.Census G a k (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a k).card S → Eq S (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a k)

concepts.description:
A valid sequence of counts and a final census omitting the target exist
exactly when the target is unreachable from the source.
concepts.sourceText:

/-!

title: Correctness of nonreachability certificates
type: lemma
---
A valid sequence of counts and a final census omitting the target exist

concepts.title: Bounded reachability
concepts.description:
A directed graph on $N$ vertices is given by its Boolean adjacency matrix.
A walk may repeat vertices. The recursive reachability test divides the
length bound in two and enumerates possible middle vertices.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Logic.Relation

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

/-!
---
title: Bounded reachability
type: definition
---
A directed graph on $N$ vertices is given by its Boolean adjacency matrix.
A walk may repeat vertices. The recursive reachability test divides the
length bound in two and enumerates possible middle vertices.
-/

namespace Lax362205.Reachability

abbrev Graph (N : ℕ) := Fin N → Fin N → Bool

inductive Walk {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) : ℕ → α → α → Prop
  | nil (a : α) : Walk R 0 a a
  | tail {n : ℕ} {a b c : α} : Walk R n a b → R b c → Walk R (n + 1) a c

def Within {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) (n : ℕ) (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∃ k ≤ n, Walk R k a b

def Reachable {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a b : Fin N) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => G u v = true) a b

def search {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) : ℕ → Fin N → Fin N → Bool
  | 0, a, b => decide (a = b) || G a b
  | k + 1, a, b => (List.finRange N).any fun m => search G k a m && search G k m b

end Lax362205.Reachability

concepts.title: Correctness of rejection by counting
concepts.description:
On a space-bounded computation, counting certifies rejection precisely when
there is no accepting computation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.ConfigurationCounting

/-!
---
title: Correctness of rejection by counting
type: lemma
---
On a space-bounded computation, counting certifies rejection precisely when
there is no accepting computation.
-/

namespace Lax362205.Rejection

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines ConfigurationCounting

axiom correct (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) (hs : M.UsesSpace w s) :
  RejectsByCounting M w s ↔ ¬ M.Accepts w

end Lax362205.Rejection

  M.UsesSpace w s → Iff (Lax362205.ConfigurationCounting.RejectsByCounting M w s) (Not (M.Accepts w))

concepts.title: The next reachable layer
concepts.description:
A vertex belongs to the next layer precisely when it is the source or has
an incoming edge from the current layer.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax362205.Counting

/-!
---
title: The next reachable layer
type: lemma
---
A vertex belongs to the next layer precisely when it is the source or has
an incoming edge from the current layer.
-/

namespace Lax362205.SuccessorLayer

open Lax362205.Reachability Counting

axiom successor {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a v : Fin N) (k : ℕ) :
  v ∈ layer G a (k + 1) ↔ v = a ∨ ∃ u ∈ layer G a k, G u v = true

end Lax362205.SuccessorLayer

statements.signature:
successor : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax362205.Reachability.Graph N) (a v : Fin N) (k : Nat),
  Iff (SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a (instHAdd.hAdd k 1)) v)
    (Or (Eq v a)
      (Exists fun u => And (SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax362205.Counting.layer G a k) u) (Eq (G u v) Bool.true)))

proofs.description: An exact census makes the negative test exhaustive.
The counting machine accepts the complement and preserves a logarithmic space bound.
Apply the nonreachability certificate to each possible accepting configuration.
The vertices classified positively are exactly the next layer.
Induct from the singleton initial layer through the certified counting steps.

Compile the sequential path and census loops to a finite Turing machine.
Every branch halts and every register has logarithmic length.
A finite subset with the same cardinality is the entire layer.
Apply complement closure in both directions and use double complementation.
The final exact census contains every reachable vertex, so omitting the target certifies nonreachability.
Remove the last edge of a nonempty walk; the empty walk ends at the source.
